summary:
Build 6 (commit eda347d, reviewed as d39e278..eda347d) rebuilds the look to the blog design in .taad/look.json and adds the author byline the look calls for. The person's restart asked for "the author and date". The look's foundation and its "Author byline" component spell out the markup and its fallback states: a missing users row or a failed read shows the date only, never an error. The builder declared the new store read.

What I read and found:
- **internal/store/signin.go:29-41.** `Store.User` reads github_id, login and avatar_url by id. sql.ErrNoRows becomes ok=false with no error, and any other error is wrapped.
- **internal/server/reader.go:84-88 and 177-186.** `readerData.Author` is filled only when the state is still found and an owner is configured. A failed read is logged with slog.Warn and leaves Author zero, so the page is never made unavailable for it. readBranch and TestThreadTenThousandTiming build readerData without Author, and branch.html prints no author.
- **report.html:3.** The span is drawn only `{{if .Author.Login}}` and the login is escaped. It is the same on / and on /reports/<slug>, so TestReaderPagesShareOneLayout still holds.
- **site.css (289 lines).** It keeps line 1, the light-dark() hex tokens (same names, so the token tests are unedited), the hidden guard (:59), every pinned rule text (`.login {`, `.body {`, `.replies {`, `.replies[hidden]`, `#feedback-sent:target`, the `.comments, .feedback, .feedback-inbox {` rule with vertical margins only, and the other pinned textarea, feedback and inbox rules), the literal thread indent (:245), edges written as a literal width and style with a *-color longhand, Canvas only on iframe (:207), and no '@'. The old orphaned '·' rule on All reports is gone.
- **probe.js:30 and look_test.go:599.** These add and require a 'meta' avatar kind.
- **author_test.go** covers the owner with and without an avatar, escaping, an owner who never signed in, no configured owner, and a failing users read (still a 200 with no author).
- **user_test.go** covers no row, the first sign-in, and a newer sign-in.

What I ran:
- `go vet ./internal/server/ ./internal/store/` is clean.
- TestReportPageNamesTheAuthor, TestUserReadsWhatSignInLastSaw, TestThreadFitsPhoneWidth (244 px at level 5 at 360), TestReaderPagesShareOneLayout and TestStylesheetTokens pass.
- `go test -count=1 -p 4 ./...` with CHROME_BIN set exits 0. Every package is ok, including internal/server at 51 s, which runs TestEveryScreenIsDesigned and TestReportFrameKeepsItsOwnCanvas, and every tests/acceptance package.
- Fitness holds all 45 rules.
- gofmt -l on the committed Go blobs is clean.
- No test process was left running.

One stale comment is new to this build: look_test.go:597-598 still names three avatar kinds while the loop under it requires four. The waived items (O-027 to O-036) are still in the code as filed, and I did not file them again.

Second round: The adversarial pass over build 6 (d39e278..eda347d) found nothing new to file. The build adds no parser, regular expression or reader of a text format. Its new boundaries are Store.User, the author read in renderReader, the meta line in report.html, the probe's 'meta' avatar kind and the CSS rewrite.

- **Store.User** (store/signin.go:29-41). The users columns are `login TEXT NOT NULL` and `avatar_url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` (migrations/0001_identity.sql:5-10), and no later migration rebuilds them. A NULL scan error cannot happen, so an owner without an avatar takes the no-image branch, which author_test.go:53-57 pins.
- **Failure paths in Store.User.** ErrNoRows becomes ok=false. Any other error, a cancelled request context included, is wrapped and returned.
- **The author read in renderReader** (reader.go:177-186). It runs only while state is still found, so an earlier votes, thread or own-feedback failure skips it. A read error is logged and leaves Author zero; the status, the open count and the rest of the page are unchanged.
- **Config.** OwnerGitHubID is validated as positive at startup. 0 occurs only in tests, which author_test.go covers.
- **Lock and gap.** No check is made under a lock and later retaken.
- **The meta line** (report.html:3). It is drawn only when `.Author.Login` is set. GitHub logins cannot be empty, and sign-in refuses an empty login.
- **Escaping.** html/template escapes the login (pinned by `the-<b>owner`) and sanitises the avatar src. A host the CSP refuses draws the ::after cover.
- **Same bytes on both reader pages.** / and /reports/<slug> get identical bytes, and TestReaderPagesShareOneLayout passes.
- **The probe's 'meta' kind** (probe.js:30) matches only img.avatar inside .meta. The branch page's .meta holds no avatar, and admin pages have no .meta.
- **CSS edge cases I followed:**
  - The composer flex column (site.css:235-236) stretches the comment and feedback labels. It also stretches the reply textarea, which is a direct child of its form (comments.html:17-19), so the textarea is never shrink-to-fit.
  - The All reports flex column with `order` (site.css:259-269) changes only the visual order. The DOM text order the e002 readers parse is unchanged, and the e002 packages pass.
  - `.comments > .comment + .comment` (site.css:243) adds only vertical space, and TestThreadFitsPhoneWidth still reports 244 px at level 5 at 360.
- **Evidence from round one still stands:** the full suite exits 0 with CHROME_BIN set, Fitness holds all 45 rules, and gofmt and vet are clean.

Reading pass: I read every range the engine listed with numbered Reads. Nothing in them is new to file.

**internal/server/reader.go:20-101**
- `pageData.ThreadScript()` returns false (line 33), and `readerData.ThreadScript()` returns HasReport (line 94).
- The comment above the latter says the found home, report and branch pages load the script and the empty and unavailable pages do not. That still matches what the code returns.
- The new `Author store.User` field (lines 84-88) and its doc match renderReader:177-186.

**internal/server/testdata/look/probe.js:1-302**
- The new 'meta' kind (line 30) is tested after 'byline'. The only `.meta` that holds an avatar is the author byline in report.html.
- The other judgements are unchanged and match the obligations they discharge: fit against the requested width (101-109), painted-only default checks (116-153), roles (155-188), the sidebar (190-205), cap width with atCap (207-219), contrast and forced states (224-280), and hidden states (283-299).

**.taad/look.json:1-802**
This is the design for this build. I held its tokens, components, layout and foundation against site.css. The new code follows it:
- Token values (site.css:4-55, under unchanged names).
- The transparent header (:171) and the 1.5rem serif brand (:176).
- The Author byline: `.author` (:202), `.meta .avatar` at 1.75rem with margin-right (:155, :203), and the 44rem centred meta line (:201).
- The pill buttons (:82, :103) and the composer flex column (:235-237).
- The letter card (:221-223) and the reactions row with its middle dots (:210-214).
- The comment rhythm (:242-244) and serif bodies (:250).
- The archive's date-first order and the legend as a footnote (:257-269).
- The report sheet at 60rem (:206) and the frame at --radius-sm with Canvas (:207).
- Tabular figures only in the admin (:124, :135, :215).
- The 38rem reading measure (:193, :205).

The look's foundation also names the report.html author span, which is where this build departs from the earlier frozen-body design, and the builder declared it.

Evidence from round one still stands: the full suite exits 0 with CHROME_BIN set, Fitness holds all 45 rules, gofmt and vet are clean, and the single stale comment at look_test.go:597-598 is already filed.

findings.claim: The comment above the avatar-kind check says an avatar was looked at 'in the header, in a byline and in a Blocked users heading (2rem, not 24 px)'. This build made the loop below it, at line 599, also require the 'meta' kind (the author byline under the report title), and byline avatars are now 1.75rem, so they are not the only kind besides the heading that differs from 24 px. The comment describes the old three-kind check.
